html:
At Kortrijk in Flanders on 11 July 1302, a militia of Flemish townsmen on foot defeated an army of French knights. Hundreds of gilded spurs were taken from the dead knights and hung in a church, giving the battle its name.

The king of France had occupied the rich county of Flanders, whose weaving towns, such as Bruges and Ghent, depended on English wool. In May 1302 the people of Bruges rose and killed the French they could find. At Kortrijk the Flemish infantry, armed with pikes and spiked clubs, held a line behind ditches and streams, and the charging knights were trapped and cut down.

It was one of the first great victories of infantry over mounted knights in medieval Europe. 11 July is the holiday of the Flemish Community of Belgium, and the battle became a symbol of the Flemish movement. It came decades before the Battle of Sluys.
